title: Retry: make planning a real per-item pass that flags vague requests
summary: Retry job hem1: replace default-filled plan fields with a deterministic per-item planning pass that flags and holds back underspecified requests, and add an `athena plan` command that prints the coordinated plan. The earlier rejection was a full verifier disk plus one criterion lacking cited commands, so the design is kept and every behavior criterion must cite commands that ran.

defaults_applied.how: New cargo tests; clippy and fmt --check clean.
Behavior criteria exercised via cargo test and cargo run, citing commands.
Criteria check the gate firing, not that fields exist.
Plan command states explicitly when nothing is open.
Environment preflight excluded as a separate change.
Docs and decision entry written for outside readers.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: retry the rejected planning job hem1 as typed; the audience is the user and the verifier, who judge whether the refusal gate fires on real vague requests.

The earlier failure was a full verifier disk (environment) plus one major finding that criterion 7 cited no command; the work itself is not known to be defective, and the earlier 743-test pass suggests the approach was sound.
The environment-preflight/unverified-state work proposed by the introspection is a separate change and is not included here, per the small default and because the typed request takes precedence.
Planning pass is deterministic code (no model call), which the docs must say.
Retry may reuse the earlier design: infer_rung with a tighter word list to address the nit.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test`: a new test shows an unread request with no bullets and no path-like words (e.g. 'make it better') is flagged underspecified, the flag names the missing field, and the item is not in Plan::order.
Run `cargo test`: a new test shows a request's first line is no longer copied into acceptance; only explicit acceptance bullets or a reading's criteria fill it.

Run `cargo test`: a new test shows a non-proposal job's rung is inferred from its request or reading, or flagged missing; it is never silently Implementation, and an item with no determinable rung is refused.
Run `cargo test`: tests assert open_questions are filled for a read and an unread request, including a touched path that does not exist and an unresolved referenced job.
Run `cargo test`: a test shows two open items naming the same path get a dependency or different groups, and items with disjoint touches share a group.

Run `cargo test`: a drain test with RealSteps over a records fixture with one specified and one vague queued item shows the vague one in Report::refused with a reason and not run; the specified one runs.

Run `cargo run -- plan` (or the equivalent new command): it prints order, parallel groups, and each item's goal, rung, acceptance, open questions, dependencies, touches, plus flagged items with reasons; with nothing open it says so explicitly. The verifier's evidence must cite the commands that ran.
Files touched outside plan.rs, reading.rs and drain.rs (display.rs, main.rs, etc.) are named in the docs or decision entry; the docs/decisions.md tradeoff about the gate rarely firing is updated.
`cargo clippy` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes; no secrets or personal data added.

Docs state plainly whether the planning pass is deterministic code or calls a model, and whether plan::trace/GapLog audit is wired to records or still follow-up; they also note unread free-text requests are refused until read, and the steward may need bullets.

out_of_scope: Verifier environment preflight, disk cleanup, and the unverified-environment verdict state (separate change)
Wiring plan::trace/GapLog audit to records unless trivial
Calling a model inside the planning pass
departures: Larger multi-crate change than the typical job, so cost and time are above the reference; the prior failure was environmental, so pass probability is near the reference.
